brief: Goldman's weekly US rates note frames the week around a hawkish FOMC: the Fed hiked 25bp unanimously to 3.75-4.00%, and Chair Warsh's non-consensus hawkish delivery hit the front end, twist-flattened the curve, and cheapened the terminal rate 15bps. Desks argue a higher starting point now means fewer subsequent hikes even as the hawkish tone lowers the bar for an October move, contingent on the next CPI print; Warsh's higher-neutral-rate framing plus a bigger buyback program is expected to anchor the 15-20y sector. Internationally, the BoE held at 3.75% despite three dissenting hawks, with QT tweaks and a Gilt-sale pause supporting duration, while the BoJ hiked to 1.25% yet the yen weakened on doubts about further tightening pace. Treasuries sold off Friday (2y 4.744%, 10y ~5%) as G4 duration supply rises to ~$93mn/bp next week against a fresh 20-30y buyback announcement. Separately, Goldman raised its 2027 AI-related hyperscaler debt issuance forecast to $420bn from $400bn, citing long-end crowding that partly motivates the buyback.
